subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should OpenClaw mobile apps support arbitrary per-gateway custom HTTP headers for authenticating proxies, and should the linked iOS and Android PRs be the canonical implementation path after owner/security proof?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but accepting credential-bearing pre-Gateway headers sets mobile secure-storage, diagnostics-redaction, reserved-header, TLS, and gateway-only attachment policy that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review and land platform PRs after proof
options.body: Treat the linked iOS and Android PRs as the implementation path once owner/security review, real behavior proof, and mergeability are satisfied.

options.title: Narrow to typed proxy auth first
options.body: Limit mobile support to a smaller Basic/Bearer/fixed-header contract before accepting arbitrary header name/value pairs.

options.title: Defer mobile proxy headers
options.body: Keep authenticated-proxy mobile access unsupported for now and document operator alternatives such as VPN/Tailscale or bypass rules.

recommendation.title: Review and land platform PRs after proof
recommendation.body: Treat the linked iOS and Android PRs as the implementation path once owner/security review, real behavior proof, and mergeability are satisfied.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the canonical issue and both linked platform PRs and is also present in recent mobile gateway connection history.
